title: Tobias Goodbarrel
dek: A halfling builder and main Ale-Chemy Knight whose welcome includes food, maps and a real choice about joining. His patience has limits: he challenges Melian after an attack, then turns to removing bodies before children can see them.

facts.Defining care: Safety, orientation, work and informed choice
facts.Status: Seen again in October 2026; earlier absence unexplained

body:
Tobias Goodbarrel can put food in front of a stranger, explain a map and find a reason to take the bodies off the street after a fight. He can also lose patience with a town leader who seems to be withholding the truth. A halfling builder and one of the three main Ale-Chemy Knights, alongside Farkur and Ryvyt, he offers practical help without becoming an endlessly agreeable host.

First, a safe place to sit

Tobias introduces himself to Fredrick, tells him to sit and rest, and assures him that he is safe. Before explaining factions or bounties, he offers food and ale and asks how the newcomer arrived.

He also asks about family and whether anyone is trying to capture or kill Fredrick. The question seeks context: an arrival can carry danger, separation or loss. Tobias then accompanies him toward Pristinia, turning advice into an escort.

A halfling’s dignity and chosen restraint

Tobias is a stout, bald halfling in armor who hates being mistaken for a dwarf. Fredrick’s mistake makes him visibly furious; he insists that he is a halfling and grips a log hard enough for the bark to crack.

After the apology, Tobias relaxes, acknowledges how much Fredrick has been through and returns to questions about the map. Hospitality is a choice he makes while angry. His kindness does not erase his wish to be seen correctly.

Maps, shops and practical choices

Tobias explains the general store, armor and weapons, the apothecary, an adventurer-run magic store and the emerging economy. He repeatedly asks whether Fredrick has questions about the map.

Orientation gives Fredrick ways to choose work, travel, danger and a possible home. Tobias does not assume that a newcomer already understands either the geography or how people make a living.

Independence before recruitment

Tobias describes the Knights as a loose organization intended to help adventurers become independent of any one town. He thinks Fredrick may be interested, but explicitly avoids pushing too hard: get steady, see what is available, then approach the Knights when ready.

Protection agreements carry expected standards of behavior. At this stage, Tobias says those standards are not fully formalized because nobody has abused the system. His account shows an institution developing obligations and norms, rather than a complete written charter.

Making advancement accessible

Tobias discusses sponsored Training Dungeon runs with Farkur and recognizes that newcomers struggle to enter the skill economy. Crafting, harvesting, gathering, town jobs and adventurer calls offer different routes to earning and becoming established.

When Fredrick asks what ten gold means, Tobias translates the sum into two healer’s kits or twenty rations. These are prices in that conversation, rather than a promise about every shop or later period.

He considers Fredrick’s build, agility, weapons and apparent style, suggesting that information bounties may suit him better than material work. Advice fits the person instead of requiring every newcomer to follow one path.

Knowing who knows more

Tobias repeatedly directs Fredrick toward Master Fenwick for Eovar knowledge, Thieves Guild contacts and public material bounties at his tower’s notice board. He admits when he is not fully informed.

He also describes Fenwick’s difficult attempt to organize an adventurers’ guild and suspects that the Ale-Chemy Knights may offer another way to pursue coordination. That suspicion belongs to Tobias; it does not establish Fenwick’s intentions or a merger of organizations.

Giving the Silver Spire a lasting shape

At Fenwick’s Wizarding Tower, later the Silver Spire, Tobias’s role as a builder becomes concrete. Fenwick praises his work during an early tour and later entrusts him with house-sitting during an absence.

The rooms Tobias helps construct give Eovar places for baths, shelter, healing and public gathering. His contribution joins the tower’s physical permanence to the welcome he offers newcomers: a place can keep helping people after its makers leave.

A route into the world’s unfinished problems

Tobias warns Fredrick about serious conflict between the Eovar Thieves Guild and adventurers, then gives him a contact who may know more. Warnings come with something useful to do next.

He describes a major BLT bounty involving pirates, murdered guardians and a stolen relic tied to defense against Death. He also mentions attacks on Melian and suggests Erebus as an investigative contact. These are reports Tobias relays, not proof that Fredrick completes an investigation or resolves the bounty.

January 2025 · a competent guide

In difficult woodland, Tobias leads the party and physically clears disruptive plant life. He is described as good-natured and a competent guide whose work makes navigation easier.

His questions about camping, rest and safety fit the same care he shows an arrival. Practical field ability supports his hospitality: he can help people reach a destination as well as explain it.

15 December 2024 · answering winter hunger

At the Common Man, Tobias orders ale and joins the civic room of workers, farmers, musicians and adventurers. When failed harvest help and dwindling winter stores become clear, he volunteers for the hunt that forms.

His response answers an immediate material need. It does not establish that the Knights already formally exist at that date or give him an invented rank.

His welcome to Fredrick gives the Knights’ wider history a practical threshold: newcomer support can be performed by someone other than Farkur. The later workshop and public-works network extends the same effort to make skills and opportunities accessible.

An absence that does not erase the work

By 8 December 2025, Tobias is described as missing again. The causes of those absences remain unresolved; the later October scenes below establish his return to activity. Later accounts credit the Knights with Gael’s market without establishing Tobias’s individual contribution.

His earlier work continues to matter through the people who received safety, maps, economic advice and contacts. Faction enthusiasm can bias his recommendations, and informal protection needs clearer rules, but his refusal to pressure Fredrick preserves a real choice about belonging.

Seen again, and traveling to Gael

The later posting record finds Tobias active again: he leaves materials at Ryvyting Creations, then arrives in Gael with Fenwick and Minerva. His earlier absence remains unexplained. A witnessed later appearance answers whether he is still missing at this stage without supplying the missing journey.

He reunites warmly with Ryvyt and joins him and Severina in the Plains. Tobias accepts their field advice, fights butterfly swarms and shares their eventual return toward the Tower after fog frustrates the hunt. He speaks of helping the building effort with smaller tasks. These scenes do not assign him sole credit for Gael’s market or turn a plan for a town into a completed settlement.

Scenes in sequence

These selected scenes preserve what was knowable when people acted. Dates below identify source postings in UTC; they do not supply an in-world calendar. A later appearance does not settle present status.

  1. 2024-11-26 · quest

    A familiar place in the tavern

    Tobias returns to the Common Man with his silvered flail and sits down to order ale.

    Known at this stage
    The scene places him among a town in unusually good spirits.
    Consequence
    His adventuring equipment and ordinary enjoyment coexist in the same moment.
    Still unresolved
    The flail and the tavern scene alone do not establish an institutional rank or founding claim.

    Receipt 1

  2. 2025-02-24 · compatible RP

    A welcome made practical

    Tobias offers food and directs Fredrick toward Herb’s rations.

    Known at this stage
    The newcomer needs immediate help and orientation.
    Consequence
    The Knights’ history includes personal welcome as well as expeditions.
    Still unresolved
    An offered meal does not establish an oath, recruitment or completed membership.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2

The men looking for Melian

At the Common Man, Tobias first treats the strangers seeking Melian as a source of tavern amusement. He jokes about a disappointed lover, watches Herb’s concerned reactions and then loses patience with information arriving a little at a time. His demand for a straight account helps the company see that the men’s explanation is a cover story.

He readies his flail, considers how much damage a tavern fight could cause and edges toward a suspected spellcaster. When the danger moves outside and fighting begins, he calls for captives if possible because they might provide information. He attacks, hurries toward Melian’s attacker and later oversees the search of the bodies. The company finds rings and a terse written instruction, but one antagonist escapes. Neither the clues nor Tobias’s confidence identifies the ultimate employer.

An offer of drinks he does not want

Afterward, Melian says she hoped the encounter would reveal who burned her home and tried to kill her. Tobias asks why she did not fight if she can protect herself. Her answer, that the town pays the adventurers to do it, angers him. He says he was brought here against his will and asks for a way home rather than another duty. The claim that the gods kidnapped him is Tobias’s account of his situation, not a new ruling on every arrival.

Melian offers drinks. Tobias avoids her gaze and concludes that the town’s leaders are withholding the full story. He chooses another task instead: ask where the bodies can be taken, so children will not find them in the street. Directed to the undertaker, he prepares to move them. His displeasure remains in the scene; the practical act does not establish that he and Melian have reconciled.

The halfling in the barrel

Another town alarm catches Tobias looking for a treat after dinner. He meets Farkur’s mechanical wolf, follows the warning of an attack and takes his place in the preparations. He identifies himself as a front-line fighter, brings a barrel out of a building and trusts Farkur as the company divides its work. He also offers spare fire and healing supplies to anyone who needs them.

Then he sits in the barrel and watches through its eyeholes. A roar from another part of the fighting does not immediately draw him out; he waits until he can see the threat on his own side. When he finally jumps out, he does so shouting. He fights the ape-like attackers with his morningstar, runs alongside Farkur and tries a javelin against another creature.

The narrator records the last enemy falling, followed by a disembodied threat of worse attacks. Tobias’s improvised hiding place has been useful in a battle won by the company. It gives a less solemn view of the same practical habits found in his building and welcome work: use what is at hand, share what can help and be ready to move.

profile.personality: Hospitable, resourceful and able to restrain anger without losing it. He minds being mistaken for a dwarf, can make a barrel into a fighting position and resents explanations that make adventurers seem like disposable labor. Care for a newcomer and removal of bodies from a public street remain beside those frustrations.
profile.achievements: Helped build the Silver Spire and was trusted to house-sit it. Gives Fredrick safety, orientation, practical prices, work choices and contacts. Discusses sponsored advancement with Farkur, guides woodland travel, volunteers against winter hunger, fights in the town’s defense and returns to activity in the later Gael scenes. Neither founder status nor his individual contribution to every market project is established.
profile.relationships: Farkur and Ryvyt are fellow main Knights. Fenwick trusts his work and is a referral for Eovar, intelligence and bounties. Fredrick receives help before any pressure to join. A quarrel with Melian preserves his wish for honest answers; her offer of drinks does not supply a documented reconciliation.
